correctness.rationale: No nontranslated pair of triples has a three-term time slice. Every matching unordered pair of edges determines one and only one two-term time slice (match oriented differences; odd p rules out a second alignment). Thus E counts double slices and there are 9−E active slices. A singleton never vanishes and a double vanishes at at most one frequency by injectivity of its nontrivial Fourier character. For p≥7 a nonprogression has all three edge classes distinct; a progression of step d has multiplicities 2 at [d] and 1 at [2d]. Two unmatched progressions cannot share both classes: reversed multiplicities would require 4d=±d. Hence E≤3. For the frequency-zero binary sign equations the left sides are distinct; a three-way dependence requires all three edges of each triangle once, so both triples share all three distinct classes. To see that this determines the triples up to reflection and translation, orient representatives of the three edge classes to sum to zero. Any two closing sign choices not global reversals could be made to differ in exactly one sign, forcing 2d=0. Permuting the oriented steps around the triangle changes its vertex set only by translation or reflection. Outside the dependent case all equations can be solved. In the reflected case the product of the three directed complex ratios would be 1=−z^M for a p-th root z, impossible, regardless of which frequency is chosen in each row. Any two sign equations are solvable, proving the exact penalty. At p=5 all triples are progressions in two orbits, interchanged by dilation; for {0,1,2} and {0,1,3}, the claimed signs cancel the slices 0,1,2,4. For p≥7 that support pair instead has E=3 and is ordinary. Counting unique progression centers gives p(p−1)(p−5)/6 nonprogressions, each with p distinct reflected translates disjoint from its own orbit. Independent finite replay enumerated all ordered nontranslated pairs at p=5,7,11,13 by computing the nine differences and the matching edge counts, obtaining 50, 980, 25410, 78078 pairs and 0,98,1210,2704 exceptions. Enumerating the 64 sign patterns for representative pairs and testing exact cyclotomic vanishing by reducing integer coefficient vectors modulo 1+z+⋯+z^(p−1) gave minima 21 (p=5), 39 and 40 (ordinary and reflected p=7), and 63 (ordinary p=11). Finite evidence corroborates the proof but does not establish the all-prime theorem. The frozen checker was not executed.

value.rationale: Prescribing the apertures is natural when the occupied sites cannot be changed. A pair-specific minimum and explicit binary-phase attainment are useful information unavailable from total-support bounds. The exact one-zero obstruction isolates a geometric invariant that matters even for unrestricted complex coefficients, and the count describes how prevalent it is. This is not just an improved global lower bound or a finite enumeration.
